question: What relative contents of N-5 and N-6 did the lignite char have after fast pyrolysis at 800 °C?
trap: the raw lignite's 51% / 26% or the sawdust char's 42% / 40%
rendered:
According to page 5 of the document: 
"For the LC sample pyrolyzed at 500 °C, the relative content of N-5 decreased, whereas N-6 and N-Q increased slightly (Fig. 4e). 
During fast pyrolysis at 800 °C, the N-A in SD completely decomposed (Fig. 4c). 
The resulting char-N distribution was dominated by N-5 (42%) and N-6 (40%).
As for the LC char pyrolyzed at 800 °C, as shown in Fig. 4f, char-N consisted of N-5, N-6, and N-Q, while N-X was completely volatilized."

The relative contents of N-5 and N-6 in the lignite char after fast pyrolysis at 800 °C are 29% and 45%, respectively.
